rows.subtype: Plans and packages compared with a bad option in the mix [Receiver]
rows.description: An adult comparing insurance or broadband plans finds one option oddly poor and notices it makes another look excellent, then pauses to ask what they need without it.

rows.description: A buyer covers up the option nobody would pick, compares the rest against their own budget and needs, and decides with a written list rather than the layout of the offer.

rows.description: A child who announced "I am the doctor" refuses to change the game even when it stops being fun, because going back on a spoken word feels wrong.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student who told the class he would win the race trains harder and will not skip practice; having said it aloud, he wants his actions to match his word.

rows.subtype: Stuck in a choice already paid for [Actor]
rows.description: A young adult keeps attending a course they dislike because months and fees are spent and friends were told; consistency outweighs present judgment, and quitting feels like admitting error.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: An adult accepts that the earlier decision was made with less information, explains the change plainly, and uses commitments on purpose for good habits without being trapped by old ones.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22

rows.subtype: Small request opens the way to a bigger one [Actor]
rows.description: A child asks a parent for just a few minutes of a game, then a few more, then the whole evening; each small yes makes the next feel like a natural continuation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Signing a tiny pledge, then being asked for more [Receiver]
rows.description: A teenager who agreed to a small online pledge finds it harder to refuse a larger follow-up; having said yes once, saying no would feel inconsistent with who they claimed to be.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Refusing a huge favour, then feeling bound by a smaller one [Receiver]
rows.description: After turning down a very large request, a young adult feels an urge to accept the smaller "compromise" that follows, as if the other side has conceded and it is now their turn.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Asking whether it would be a yes as a first request [Response]
rows.description: An adult facing a step-by-step or big-then-small ask pauses and asks "would I agree if this were the first thing requested?", and is free to say no to the current step.
